attribution_of_the_two_reds.verdict: AILANG toolchain defect (--strict-bytecode compiler/VM bug), not a milestone code or test defect
evidence: `make test` run: `strict VM ... | interpreter ... | closed form ...` for the original `scripted()` matches (21.392852753780428 == interpreter, within 1e-9 of closed form) -- the pre-existing strict check is unaffected.
The new off-axis strict check crashes: `Error: bytecode execution failed: vm: vm: GET_FIELD: index 3 exceeds field count 3 (in sim/core.turn at sim/core.ail:21, ip 0, op GET_FIELD)`.

Negative control 1 (interpreter): `ailang run --quiet --package-dir sim --entry scriptedOffAxis --args-json 300 sim/core.ail` succeeds, returns 27.637939595105987, matching the closed form (27.637939595106303) within 1e-9.
Negative control 2 (plain --bytecode, non-strict): also succeeds with the same value.

Minimal isolated repro (self-contained ~20-line file, no dependency on this milestone's own code): a local 5-field record type embedding the package's `Vec3` and calling the published `pkg/sunholo/relativity/optics.normalize` inside a nested record-construction expression. Under `--strict-bytecode` it crashes: `GET_FIELD: index 3 exceeds field count 3 (in pkg/sunholo/relativity/optics.dot ...)`. Under the interpreter and plain --bytecode it correctly returns 1.0. Reproduced 3 separate ways while bisecting (with/without the if/else chain, with/without normalize()) -- the crash site moves between `core.turn` and the package's `optics.dot`, but the defect class (record field-count/index mismatch at ip 0 of the entered function under --strict-bytecode only) is constant.

Conclusion: this is a compiler/codegen defect in AILANG v0.45.0's --strict-bytecode path for record field layout across a package boundary; the milestone's own code and tests are written exactly as the spec and sprint plan direct.

attribution_of_the_two_reds.verdict: AILANG toolchain defect (nondeterministic plain --bytecode VM execution), not a milestone code or test defect, not a flaw in the test
evidence: 6 standalone re-runs of `make parity-offaxis`: 3 pass ('identical (17 lines)'), 3 fail ('.godot/tmp/offaxis_vm.txt .godot/tmp/offaxis_interp.txt differ: char 265, line 3') -- same diff location every failure.

Isolated the fault to the VM alone (not a VM-vs-interpreter drift): ran `ailang run --bytecode ... < tests/fixtures/offaxis.ndjson` 20 times with NO interpreter comparison at all. Got 2 distinct stable output hashes: 15/20 one hash, 5/20 another -- the VM is not even self-consistent across repeated invocations of the identical static input file.

Negative control: the pre-existing 601-line v1.0 parity script (hello + 600 step commands, never touches `heading`) run 15x through the VM alone: 15/15 identical -- no nondeterminism when `turn()` is never invoked.

Shrunk to a minimal 3-line NDJSON (hello; one step with a heading turn; quit), 30 VM-only runs: 25/30 correct (tick 1, heading turned), 5/30 silently wrong -- returns the untouched initial state (tick 0, default heading) with status:'ok' (not a rejection code), i.e. the VM sometimes evaluates `turn()`'s `changed` guard as false when it is actually true and silently no-ops an accepted command.

This is the non-crashing sibling of the --strict-bytecode GET_FIELD bug above: same code path (turn() constructing a record that embeds the package Vec3 type), but under non-strict bytecode the out-of-bounds/misrouted field access doesn't trip a bounds check -- it silently reads a stale/wrong value instead of crashing.

Practical mitigation already present in this milestone: bridge/sim_bridge.gd's step() independently checks `tick == before.tick + 1` on every 'ok' reply and fails bounded+cleanly (bad_response) on mismatch, so this VM bug would not silently corrupt live gameplay through the bridge -- only the raw NDJSON VM-vs-interpreter parity harness (which bypasses that guard by design, to catch exactly this class of drift) exposes it. The test is doing its job correctly.

recommendation: FAIL (hard fail on Tests Pass; score 59/100 would also be below threshold on its own). The implementation itself is high quality and matches the design doc and sprint plan closely -- do NOT send this back to the executor for rework; the two reds are independently confirmed AILANG v0.45.0 toolchain defects (a --strict-bytecode record-field-index compiler bug and a related non-strict-bytecode nondeterministic silent-corruption bug, both triggered by constructing a record that embeds the published package's Vec3 type inside a call into a package pure function), not defects in sim/core.ail, sim/ship.ail, or their tests. Recommended next steps: (1) file both with `ailang messages` (AILANG_STORAGE_MESSAGING=gcp, --from stapledons_godot) with the minimal repros captured in this report -- could not confirm from this sandbox whether that has already been done; (2) close out the M1.6a_SIM_PROTOCOL sprint-JSON entry as passes:false with the upstream-blocked explanation rather than leaving it null; (3) once AILANG publishes a fix (or a documented workaround such as avoiding package-typed fields inside locally-constructed records under --strict-bytecode), re-run `make test` unmodified -- no code changes to this milestone's diff should be needed; (4) separately, add one negative test for a cmd-less-but-valid-JSON message before this closes, to remove the one confirmed test-coverage gap (mutation table, last row).
